questions.q: What does 'fail fast' mean as a pipeline design principle?
options: A pipeline should only ever have one stage
A pipeline should surface a failure at the earliest possible stage and stop immediately and clearly, rather than limping forward
A pipeline should continue past a failure to see what else happens
A pipeline should never run Apex tests
questions.explain: Failing fast means stopping clearly at the first problem instead of producing confusing partial results from stages that ran after a failure nobody addressed.

questions.q: What does it mean for a pipeline stage to be idempotent?
options: It runs only once per calendar day
It can never be retried under any circumstances
Running it twice with the same input produces the same result as running it once
It always deploys to production regardless of target org
questions.explain: Idempotency means repeating a step with the same input doesn't change the outcome -- which is what makes a step safe to retry.

questions.q: Why does this lesson specifically call out 'always have a fallback' for delta deployments?
options: Because delta deployments are illegal in production orgs
Because delta deployments always run faster than full deployments with no downside
Because fallback paths are only relevant to Apex testing
Because a delta deployment can produce an incomplete or wrong manifest, so the pipeline needs a way to fall back to a full deployment rather than silently shipping a partial change
questions.explain: Delta deployments are the part of the pipeline most likely to misbehave if the diff base is wrong, so keeping a manual full-deploy fallback available is the specific safeguard this lesson calls out.

questions.q: Why does a 40-minute pipeline undermine the purpose of a 'fast feedback loop', per this lesson?
options: Because 40 minutes exceeds GitHub Actions' maximum runtime

Because the point of fast feedback is that a developer learns whether their change is good while they still remember what they changed -- a long delay defeats that almost as much as no pipeline at all
Because Apex tests cannot run for more than 10 minutes
A 40-minute pipeline has no real downside according to this lesson
questions.explain: Fast feedback matters because it keeps the pipeline's result useful to the developer while the change is still fresh in their mind -- a long wait erodes that usefulness.

questions.q: What does 'observable and debuggable' mean as applied to pipeline design in this lesson?
options: Only administrators should be able to view pipeline results
A pipeline should never produce any error messages
A pipeline should hide its logs to keep output clean
A pipeline should make its own failures easy to diagnose, with real logs per step and clear error messages surfaced where a developer will actually see them
questions.explain: An observable, debuggable pipeline surfaces real step-level logs and clear errors in a place developers actually look, rather than hiding failures in a file nobody opens.
